result.summary: The environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with commercial land use and minimal pedestrian crossing infrastructure. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crosswalks or signals across the main thoroughfare creates a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic on the main road without a marked crosswalk or refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground across the main roadway

hazards.name: Faded Pavement Markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings on the side street are significantly faded, reducing visibility to drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection across the side street

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the corner of the side street may block sight lines between pedestrians and turning drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style high-visibility crosswalks across all legs of the intersection to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a median refuge island on the main road to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to reduce the crossing distance and improve sight lines by preventing parking too close to the intersection.

result.summary: The environment is a car-oriented commercial corridor with a sidewalk but no marked pedestrian crossings or traffic calming measures. A pedestrian is visible crossing the roadway mid-block, highlighting the lack of safe infrastructure and high exposure to traffic.

hazards.name: Unmarked mid-block crossing
hazards.description: A pedestrian is seen crossing the two-lane roadway without any marked crosswalk or signage, creating high exposure to vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Left-center, pedestrian in the roadway

hazards.name: Commercial driveway conflicts
hazards.description: The continuous sidewalk is interrupted by multiple wide commercial driveways, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side, along the sidewalk and parking lot entrance

hazards.name: Lack of traffic calming
hazards.description: The wide, straight roadway design with minimal vertical elements encourages higher vehicle speeds in a commercial zone.
hazards.location_in_image: Center roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint and pedestrian warning signage to formalize crossing points.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of formal crossing infrastructure at an intersection adjacent to a gas station. While sidewalks are present, the absence of marked crosswalks, traffic controls, and lane markings creates a high-conflict environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated or protected space to cross the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the intersection

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Points
hazards.description: The gas station entrance and exit create multiple points where vehicle movements may conflict with pedestrians on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image at the gas station entrance

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb on the left side of the street may block sight lines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to improve sight lines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and slow turning vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Traffic Control Signage
interventions.description: Install stop signs or other traffic control devices to manage the right-of-way at the intersection.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane commercial corridor with significant crossing distances and no visible marked pedestrian crossings. While sidewalks are present on both sides, the environment is dominated by vehicle-centric design with long sightlines that likely encourage higher speeds.
